claims.text: The starting AlCrFeNiSi powder is homogeneous and gas-atomized.
The starting powder is sieved to a particle-size range of 10–60 μm.
The powder is dispersed in an acrylate-based photocurable resin and formed into layered green bodies by DLP printing.
The proposed intervention is continuous mechanical-pump evacuation during debinding instead of debinding in ambient air.
The proposed debinding schedule includes 1 h holds at 300 °C and 450 °C followed by heating to 500 °C.
The stated sintering boundary is 24 h of solid-state sintering at 800–1100 °C.
The stated DLP settings are a 405 nm source, 19.57 mW/cm² intensity, 100 s exposure, 70 μm layers, and 20 layers.
Oxygen-deficient debinding retains more residual carbon from the resin.
Retained carbon reduces the rate of CO and CO2 generation and associated rapid gas evolution.
Reduced gas evolution lowers internal pressure during debinding.
Lower internal pressure reduces pore formation and surface cracking.
Residual carbon promotes interfacial diffusion and interparticle bonding at lower sintering temperatures.
Oxygen-rich debinding produces surface oxides that impede consolidation.
Air-debound specimens require approximately 1100 °C to reach full consolidation.
Air-debound specimens reach approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength at 1100 °C.
Oxygen-deficient debinding will provide approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength after sintering near 1050 °C, about 50 °C below the stated air-debound requirement.
Oxygen-deficient debinding will visibly reduce surface cracking and improve interparticle bonding relative to air debinding.
Diffusion remains limited below approximately 1000 °C under the stated processing conditions.
At 1100 °C under oxygen-deficient conditions, stripe-like precipitates or other localized microstructural anomalies may form.
The possible high-temperature anomalies are attributed to insufficient oxide protection of fine particles.
